requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate. They cover each obligation in `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, and their assertions check exact outcomes. I did not read implementation source, so this judgment rests only on the supplied tests.

- **`/`-separated path and empty selector selects the root.**
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` parses `""` to an empty segment list. It also parses a multi-segment path and rejects `a//b`, `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]`, `fn[run]#0`, `use@123` and `fn[run]x`.
  - `tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts that `resolve("")` returns node 0.
- **Named segment `kind[name]`.** `fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` checks about 20 selectors across all the Rust kinds, including nested paths like `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`. For each one it asserts that the selector is produced and that it resolves back to a node with that same selector.
- **Anonymous segment `kind@hash`, first 12 hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` asserts the `use@` prefix and a length of 12. It also checks that inserting an unrelated `use` keeps the old selectors resolving, and that editing a `use` invalidates only that selector.
  - `fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` asserts that the selector equals `pair[items]/item@{identity_hash[..12]}`. It also asserts that the identity hash differs from the structural hash, and that the selector still resolves after a descendant edit.
  - `markdown_tests.rs#fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]` checks the segment shape for anonymous markdown nodes: `kind@` followed by 12 characters.
- **`#N` disambiguation by one-based source order.**
  - `fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` expects `fn[repeated]#1` and `fn[repeated]#2`, and expects the bare `fn[repeated]` to fail to resolve.
  - `fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` expects identical `use` items to end in `#1` and `#2`.
  - The parser test rejects `#0` and accepts `#2`.
- **`line` nodes are interchangeable.** `fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` shows two identical lines get the same `line@` selector. It also shows that this selector resolves, and that whitespace inside a line is ignored while removing it changes the selector.
- **Percent-encoding of `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and whitespace as UTF-8 bytes, reversibly.**
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding]` asserts the exact encoded string. The input includes a tab, a no-break space, an ideographic space and non-ASCII `é`. It asserts that decoding round-trips and that raw `/`, a raw space and a malformed `%zz` are rejected.
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]` in the Rust test covers encoding in a real outline.
  - `tests.rs#fn[profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent]` covers the malformed-escape error path.
  - `tests/search.rs#fn[outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reinterpreting_resources]` accepts `mod[a%2Fb]/fn[kept]` and rejects `fn[missing`, `fn[bad%ZZ]` and `/fn[kept]` at the address layer.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** Every exact-equality assertion on selectors, in the Rust, YAML, plain-text and markdown tests, would fail if a line number were embedded. No test does this negative check on its own, but it is covered implicitly.

I found no unacknowledged gap. The cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` is context, and the selector tests exercise it where the selector depends on it: identity-hash prefix, descendant-edit stability, and the whitespace word rule for lines.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
